item.title: Catchment hydrologic function is widely time-variant
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04079-6

How catchments convert rainfall and snowmelt into streamflow is widely time-variant, shifting from one event to the next even where successive events arrive as the same water-input type on similarly wet or dry soils, according to an analysis of ~1.7 million runoff-producing events across 4,838 catchments on six continents.
item.dc:title: Catchment hydrologic function is widely time-variant

item.title: Grazing-related disturbance decouples aboveground and belowground responses in the Eurasian meadow steppe
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04104-8

Grazing elicits contrasting biodiversity responses above and below ground, with plant communities peaking at intermediate disturbance and soil communities reorganizing in line with the stress-gradient hypothesis, based on analyses along a grazing gradient in the Eurasian meadow steppe.
